messages:
elaine: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector roll we see a hard perf regression on qwen2.5 multi-ling test (zh/en mix). p99 jumped and throughput dropped under steady-state batching. Anyone else seeing this? :thinking:

matt: Seen it on the US cluster too. p50 fine, p95 up ~40ms, p99 up ~210ms. Looks related to kernel switch to composite-kernel-v2.

elaine: Repro steps I ran: `./bench/run_infer --model qwen2p5 --kernels=composite-v2 --batch=8 --seq=1024 --langs=zh,en`
Output snippet from perf run:
```
[run] requests/sec: 85
latencies_ms: p50=72 p95=150 p99=790
gpu_util: 62% mem_copies: increased (GPU memcpy host->dev)
```

raj: Quick guess: composite-v2 changed how KV buffers are laid out for multi-heads (non-contiguous strides). Combined with tokenizer token-offset rounding for CJK we might be getting misaligned KV memcpy patterns, extra copies per head. Can you dump the KV shape prints?

elaine: Dumped during warmup; here's what we log right before attention kernel call:
```
kv.shape: (batch=8, seq=1024, heads=64, kv_dim=128)
kstride bytes: 4096
buffer_contiguous: False
selected_kernel: composite-v2/stride-optim
```

perf-bot: Attached flamegraph (short): memcpy > kernel_launch > waitEvent. Unusual spike at memcpy when seq>512.

matt: If buffer_contiguous=false then composite-v2 falls back to per-head memcpy loops. That explains extra memcopies per request. Why did buffer become non-contiguous? Tokenizer change?

elaine: We correlate with a tokenizer patch that changed subword splitting for CJK to preserve byte offsets (PR #4121). That produces different token boundary alignments for zh sentences which changed sequence packing and led to slightly different sequence lengths & packing layout. But still surprised by contiguity flip.

raj: There's a low-level allocator change too: the multi-gpu pipelining path started using segmented allocator for KV when average seq length variance > 0.35. Segmented alloc returns non-contiguous slices by design. composite-v2's fast path requires contiguous KV across heads. So new allocator + tokenizer variance = falling back to slow per-head copies.

ops-bot: Canary flagged commit 7f3d2c (allocator:segmented-alloc) as deployed to prod at 2026-03-12T03:22Z.

elaine: Quick profiler numbers after forcing contiguous allocation (local patch):
```
# with segmented alloc (bad)
p99=790ms throughput=85 rps memcpy_time=140ms
# with force-contiguous (patch)
p99=620ms throughput=110 rps memcpy_time=35ms
```

matt: Nice. So two levers: revert allocator change for qwen2p5 pipelines OR make composite-v2 accept segmented KV (hard). Short-term rollback?

sophia: Ops: we can roll allocator config back on the affected pool and roll a canary to 10% traffic. Recommend: rollback allocator + keep composite-v2 for now. Then follow-up: patch composite-v2 to accept strided KV or add an allocator hint to always return contiguous for models that need it.

raj: For the longer fix, composite-v2 can accept a 'head_stride' metadata and perform a single stride-aware memcpy (vectorized) instead of N small memcpys. I sketched a micro-optim in python to reshape host-side when building KV: `kv = np.ascontiguousarray(kv.reshape(batch, seq, heads, kv_dim).swapaxes(1,2))` — that avoids extra copies in many cases. But cost varies; need kernel-bench.

elaine: I ran a focused kernel micro-bench on a single GPU: comparing three configs (old-kernel, composite-v2 w/contig, composite-v2 w/segmented). Results:
```
old-kernel p99=470ms
composite-v2 + contig p99=480ms
composite-v2 + segmented p99=720ms
```
So composite-v2 only matches/helps when contig guaranteed.

matt: Also saw unexpected head/kv mismatch logged on some requests: `kv_head_mismatch: True` which comes from runtime sanity check. That correlates with token-pack variance: some requests ended up with kv.shape heads != model.expected_heads after pack/unpack when odd padding codepath used. We should hard-fail those earlier rather than let kernels cope.

elaine: Agreed. I pushed a small validation patch to reject non-matching kv dims and log a reproducible payload. Patch ID: patch/diagnostic/kv-validate-2301. Not rolling to prod until we have fix.

raj: For multilingual tokenizer edge-cases: CJK tokenization frequently creates higher variance in seq lengths since it doesn't merge ascii tokens the same way. Batching heuristics that pack by requested token count now produce more fragmented allocations. We should update packer to prefer contiguity for models using composite kernels.

perf-bot: Quick A/B sim (1000 requests):
A (current): p99=760ms, mediancyc=6.2 copies/req
B (force contig allocation): p99=490ms, mediancyc=1.1 copies/req

sophia: Ops plan: revert segmented-alloc on the two affected pools, enable diagnostic kv-validate, canary to 5% for 30m, measure. If green, broaden. I'll open infra ticket and schedule rollback window.

matt: Follow-ups for runtime team: (1) add allocator hint API for models (force-contiguous), (2) add stride-aware composite-kernel path, (3) tighten packer heuristics for mixed-language batches.

elaine: I'll attach the failing request payloads and micro-bench scripts in the GH issue. For now rolling back allocator on canary looks lowest-risk. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Rollback scheduled: 2026-03-13T01:15Z -> rolling to 5% canary.
